newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo platinum futures seen down before Dec expiry.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo platinum futures seen down before Dec expiry.

text.p: The Tokyo platinum futures market is likely to be hit by active selling ahead of the expiry of the spot December contract on December 18 as local investors liquidate large long positions, traders said on Tuesday.
Japanese traders have said that continuing long liquidation in the Tokyo futures market was behind the recent fall in the price of platinum in world markets.
Open interest in the spot December contract on the Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM) totalled 22,301 lots as of December 9.
This is equivalent to nearly 11.15 tonnes of platinum.
"Given the fact that there's about one week before the spot expiry, this figure is unusually high," a trader at a major trade house in Tokyo said.
"We expect active long liquidation by individual investors from late this week," the trader said.
Platinum was at a three-year low at $368.00 in London trade on Monday morning, while COMEX January platinum hit a fresh contract low at $370.00 before closing down $2.60 at $370.20.

On Tuesday, the TOCOM platinum market ended mostly higher as the weaker yen offset bearishness from the drop in New York prices. The benchmark October 1997 contract was up seven yen to 1,342 yen per gram.
The spot December ended up four yen at 1,359 yen, against 1,374 yen on December 2 and 1,392 yen on November 1.

"Japanese investors earlier this year built long orders in the platinum market, while they sold in the gold market. The remaining large positions in the platinum December contract are a by-product of that," a trader at another trade house said.
A key factor for the market is how many physical platinum deliveries local investors will take at the December's expiry next week, traders said.
"If local investors receive physical platinum deliveries, rather than liquidate their long positions, we may be able to escape from a price crash," a brokerage house trader said.
"But at this stage we don't have a clear idea about what's coming," he said.
Japan is the world's largest consumer of platinum group metals and imported 60.22 tonnes in the first 10 months of 1996, Finance Ministry data showed.
TOCOM, which was launched in January 1984, is the world's most active market for platinum.
Its volume during the January-November period totalled 6,338,132 lots, TOCOM data showed.
